newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-UK's Granada boosted by Forte deal.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-UK's Granada boosted by Forte deal.

text.p: Britain's Granada Group Plc unveiled a 33 percent half year profit rise on Wednesday as it reaped the benefits of its takeover of hotel and catering empire Forte last year.

Chairman Gerry Robinson said Granada had delivered on its promise of a 100 million pound ($160 million) annual profit improvement at Forte, acquired for 3.9 billion pounds 18 months ago after a bitter takeover battle.
Granada's pre-tax profit, excluding exceptional items climbed 33 percent to 243 million pounds in the 26 weeks to end March. The dividend was raised 10 percent to 4.66 pence per share.
Granada shares, which have risen in the past few days on anticipation of strong figures, fell 17 pence to close at 885.5 pence as the FTSE 100 index of leading shares came off recent highs.
The company said second half trading had begun encouragingly and analysts are forecasting full-year profit of 620-650 million pounds, up from 480 million.
Analysts at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson said Granada shares remained undervalued after underperforming the market by around nine percent over the past year.
But they said Granada must prove it was following a consistent disposal strategy after the Forte deal.

The company has raised over 1.3 billion pounds from disposals in the past 18 months but has decided to retain assets such as London's large Grosvenor House hotel after initially putting it up for sale.

"Investors are not used to seeing their holdings in Granada underperform and fundamentally the stock should trade at much higher levels," Dresdner Kleinwort Benson said in its research note. "However, there is a need to actually follow the set strategy," it added.
Robinson said there were more benefits to come from Forte, Britain's largest hotel group and the owner of the Meridien international brand.
"There is a tremendous upside to be had out of running that Forte business," Robinson told reporters.

Granada is lining up its first big acquisition since the Forte deal, seeking to expand in Britain's commercial television (ITV) sector by taking over northern neighbour Yorkshire-Tyne Tees Television.

Robinson told Reuters the boards of the two companies had agreed a price of 1175 pence per share for the 73 percent of Yorkshire which Granada does not own. That values Yorkshire at just over 700 million pounds.

But Robinson later stressed that the structure and timing of any deal was still to be thrashed out. "This deal is by no means finalised...It now has to be tied up in terms of detail," he told a news conference.
Despite continued press speculation Granada said it had no plans to demerge its media arm, which accounts for 25 percent of operating profit.
Granada is one of the main companies in the regionalised ITV network, broadcasting to north-west England plus London at weekends.
An acquisition of Yorkshire would allow Granada and its advertisers to reach a vast part of northern England, from Liverpool in the west to Newcastle in the east.

The move would be a further boost to the company's developing programme production arm which has recently won a contract from US network ABC to make an American version of the British crime drama series "Cracker". ($ = 0.610 British Pounds)
